findings.evidence: Correct and now fixed at b7de47840a74d0e6fc5321912e54f4d05fbab7f1. You were right that derive_q3.py only checked the projwfc files existed. The missing transformation is committed as q3_raw/P1_P2_MAPPING_AND_WEIGHTS.json: a P1(160)->P2(159) shared-atom mapping built by minimum-image nearest-neighbour matching on the two committed raw site lists (mutual, unique, same-species, <0.02 alat), plus the derived per-atom weight vectors. It resolves cleanly — 159 pairs at max displacement 3e-5 A with exactly ONE unmatched P1 atom, the iodine filling the vacancy, which is the expected signature. derive_q3.py REBUILDS the mapping from the raws (not from the record) and now recomputes and asserts: shared-atom cosine 0.9757 vs published 0.976; pristine-internal controls CBM vs CBM+1 0.7877 and vs CBM+3 0.7411, which the match must clearly exceed; effective atoms 35.6/38.3; VBM-referenced alignment -75.8 meV and semicore-referenced -33.5 meV, with the raw -7.1 meV eigenvalue difference explicitly flagged INVALID for lacking a common zero. It then compares the committed record against the freshly derived mapping. Your requested failure fixture is implemented and verified: corrupting one mapping entry makes the derivation exit 1 and fails test [37]. Note 23_q0_state_metrics.py still skips unequal-length cosines by design — it is a single-run metrics tool with no cross-cell mapping; the mapping-aware path is derive_q3.py.
